conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during this admission. Can you tell me what brought you in today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’ve been having really bad stomach pain again—same kind I always get with my pancreatitis. It started a few days ago, right after I caught a cold from my son.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Where is the pain located?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s mostly in my upper belly, right in the middle, and it goes through to my back. It comes and goes, but it’s been getting worse. I’ve been vomiting a lot—can’t keep anything down, not even pills.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That sounds very uncomfortable. Are you having any fevers, chills, or shortness of breath?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fevers or chills. Just the cold symptoms—post-nasal drip and a sore throat. But I do feel wiped out and have a headache.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’ll examine you now and we’ll get some labs. We’ll also keep you NPO—nothing by mouth—for now to let your pancreas rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your exam shows tenderness in the upper abdomen, but no signs of infection or serious complications. We’ll start your usual IV pain and nausea meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I know this routine—it usually helps after a few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs came back—your white count is normal, and there’s no sign of kidney or liver issues. We’re not seeing any complications like obstruction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. My pain is still pretty bad, though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re giving you Dilaudid every two hours as needed, along with Phenergan and Ondansetron for nausea. We’ll keep monitoring your response.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You spiked a low-grade fever last night, so we drew blood cultures. We’re watching closely for infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, I didn’t even notice. Could it be from my port? I’ve had issues before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a possibility. We did a chest X-ray this morning—your port is in good position, no signs of pneumonia. But we’ll wait for the culture results.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The blood cultures grew a gram-negative rod—Herbaspirillum species. It’s rare, but it’s likely coming from your port.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that serious? I’ve never heard of that bacteria.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It can be serious if not treated, but the good news is it’s sensitive to several antibiotics. We’re starting you on IV Zosyn for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re switching from Zosyn to IV ceftazidime. The bacteria responded better to it, and it’s safer for long-term use.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Will I need to take it at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We’ll also be doing antibiotic ‘dwells’ in your port—flushing it with ceftazidime to clear the infection from the source.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve never done that before. Is it hard?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: A visiting nurse will help you at first. We’ll teach you how to do it safely. It’s important to prevent future infections.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your repeat blood cultures are negative—great news. The antibiotics are working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. How long will I need to stay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you a few more days to finish IV antibiotics and make sure your pain is under control before discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to start advancing your diet—clear liquids today, then soft foods if you tolerate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m nervous—last time I tried to eat, I threw up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll go slow. We’ll also restart your oral pain meds and see how you do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well on the soft diet. No vomiting, and your pain is improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I actually feel hungry for the first time in days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a great sign. We’ll keep building up to your regular diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your iron levels. You’re still anemic, so we gave you an IV iron infusion to help with fatigue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been feeling so tired. I hope that helps.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood pressure has been high—up to 150s over 100. It’s likely from pain and stress. We restarted your lisinopril.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I usually take 10 mg. Is that what I’m on now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We increased it to 40 mg while you were in pain, but we’re tapering back to your usual 10 mg as your pain improves.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your INR was low when you came in, so we switched you from Coumadin to Lovenox for a few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember that from last time. When do I go back on Coumadin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re already back on it. We bridged with Lovenox until your INR was therapeutic. At discharge, you’ll take 10 mg daily for three days, then get your INR checked.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re making great progress. Pain is much better, you’re eating well, and the infection is clearing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. I just want to get home and rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning for discharge in a couple of days. We’ll make sure you’re set up with home nursing for your IV antibiotics and dwells.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need to do the dwells myself?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll do them yourself, but the nurse will train you and visit regularly. It’s every 12 hours, alternating ports.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your final blood cultures are negative. That means the bacteremia is cleared.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s wonderful. What about my pain meds at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll go home with methadone, hydromorphone for breakthrough pain, and your usual omeprazole and amitriptyline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re discharging you tomorrow. You’ll need to take ceftazidime IV twice daily for six more days and do the antibiotic dwells.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the Lovenox?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, two doses—70 mg twice tomorrow. Then stop. Continue Coumadin as directed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see your PCP soon. They’ll draw blood cultures one week after finishing antibiotics to make sure the infection is gone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re reviewing your discharge meds. You’ll also get a short course of lorazepam at night if anxiety keeps you up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been anxious about managing everything at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The home health team will help. And you’re not alone—we’re all here to support you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Final check: you’re ambulatory, alert, pain is mild, and you’re tolerating a regular diet and tube feeds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel so much better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll discharge you tomorrow morning. Make sure you have all your prescriptions and instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re cleared to go home. The nurse will set up your first home visit today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I really appreciate everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Remember: finish all antibiotics, do the dwells, check your INR, and follow up with your doctor. Call us if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’m ready to rest and get back to normal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll see you in follow-up if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you again.
